meta.titre: Cameroon's Vision 2035: government efforts across transport, farming, training and other sectors
meta.sous_theme: The aim of emergence and the government's efforts in key sectors

sections.contenu_markdown: When a power cut stops a tailor's machine in Bafoussam, or a lorry sits for hours on a broken road, small businesses lose money. Cameroon's long-term plan aims to remove problems like these so that the country can emerge as a more industrialised nation. The GCE paper asks what the government is doing in particular sectors, and which problems stand in its way. A good answer names the sector, the action and the benefit.

items: An economy grows when the total value of goods and services produced increases.
Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors form an economy.
Infrastructure includes roads, railways, ports, electricity and communications.
Foreign exchange is the money from other countries earned by exports.

sections.titre: Vision 2035: what emergence means and what the government is doing
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Vision 2035
**Vision 2035** is Cameroon's long-term development plan, which aims to make the country an **emerging** one by the year 2035. An emerging country is one whose economy is growing and becoming more industrial, with rising incomes, better infrastructure and less poverty. The plan names four general aims: to reduce poverty, to become a middle-income country, to become a newly industrialised country, and to strengthen national unity and democracy. It is carried out through shorter plans, the first called the Growth and Employment Strategy Paper (2010 to 2019) and the later National Development Strategy (2020 to 2030).

### Efforts by sector
| Sector | Problem to solve | Efforts by the government | Expected benefit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Manufacturing | Raw materials are often exported unprocessed | Encouraging local processing of timber, cocoa and cotton; industrial zones; incentives for investors | More jobs, goods made at home, higher export earnings |
| Energy | Power cuts and low supply | Building hydroelectric dams (such as Memve'ele and Lom Pangar) and a gas power plant at Kribi; extending the grid | Reliable power for factories and homes |
| Minerals | Large deposits are little used | Exploring and developing iron ore, bauxite and cobalt-nickel; agreements with mining companies | Export income and raw materials for industry |
| Transport | Poor roads, slow ports | Upgrading roads and building motorways; the Kribi deep-sea port; rail and airport improvements | Cheaper, faster movement of goods |
| Agriculture and training | Low yields; shortage of skilled workers | Modernising farming; technical and vocational schools | Food, raw materials and skilled labour |

### Problems that may delay emergence
Shortage of money, power cuts, poor roads, dependence on a few raw material exports, falling world prices, unemployment among the young, corruption and insecurity that discourages investment.

variantes.nom: Questions that ask for efforts or measures
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command is state, name or list
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give short, separate points, each naming the action and, where possible, the sector: *building dams to raise electricity supply* is better than *energy*. Count the points the question asks for and write exactly that many.

variantes.nom: Questions that ask how the government is preparing in named sectors
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question gives you sectors to treat
variantes.contenu_markdown: Take each sector in turn and use the pattern *action, then result*. Use the marks to decide the length: two marks means two clear points, or one explained point.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is discuss or explain with problems
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give a problem, explain how it slows development and, if asked, suggest a solution. Use general, factual problems and avoid taking political sides.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the government of Cameroon is trying to improve the transport sector as part of its plan to emerge by 2035. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command and the sector.
etapes.justification: Explain means that each action needs a result.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: three actions, each with a benefit.

etapes.justification: The action must be real and specific.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Roads are being upgraded and motorways are being built to link major cities.

etapes.justification: Transport covers ports as well as roads.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A deep-sea port has been built at Kribi so that larger ships can load and unload.

etapes.justification: Railways and airports show that you know the full system.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Railways and airports are being improved.

etapes.justification: Marks are given for the results of the actions.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Goods and passengers move faster and more cheaply, which supports farmers, factories and trade.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The government is upgrading roads and building motorways between the main cities, so that goods reach markets more quickly and cheaply. It has built a deep-sea port at Kribi, which allows bigger ships to load and unload and helps exports of timber and farm products. It is also improving railways and airports. With better transport, farmers can sell their produce, factories receive raw materials on time, and trade grows, which supports the aim of emerging by 2035.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing "Cameroon is already an emerging country".
items.pourquoi_faux: Emergence by 2035 is a target; the country is working towards it.
items.correction_markdown: Say that the government aims to emerge by 2035 and is carrying out measures to reach it.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving only the sector name, such as "energy", as an effort.
items.pourquoi_faux: A sector name is not an action.
items.correction_markdown: Name what is done: for example, building hydroelectric dams to increase electricity supply.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing the same effort twice in different words.
items.pourquoi_faux: Repeating a point earns only one mark.
items.correction_markdown: Choose separate actions, such as dams, a power plant and grid extension.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing about the problems when the question asks for efforts.
items.pourquoi_faux: The answer does not match the command, so it earns no marks.
items.correction_markdown: Check whether the question asks for efforts, problems or both, and answer only that.

items.pourquoi_faux: Iron ore and bauxite are minerals; dams and power plants belong to energy.
items.correction_markdown: Place hydroelectric dams under energy, and the mining of iron ore and bauxite under minerals.

items.enonce_markdown: Define the term emerging country and state two features of such a country.
items.solution_markdown:
An emerging country is one whose economy is growing fast and becoming more industrial, with improving living standards.
- Features: a growing industrial sector; rising incomes; better infrastructure; falling poverty (any two).

**Definition plus two features earns full marks.**

items.enonce_markdown: A power plan aims to raise the national electricity capacity from 800 MW to 1100 MW. (a) Calculate the increase in capacity and express it as a percentage of the original capacity. (b) Explain two ways in which a better electricity supply helps manufacturing. (The figures are for practice only.)
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Increase = 1100 - 800 = **300 MW**. Percentage increase = 300 / 800 x 100 = **37.5%**.

(b) Any two explained points:
- Factories can run machines without stoppages, so output and profits rise.
- Reliable power attracts investors, who build more factories and create jobs.
- Small workshops can use machines instead of hand tools, so they produce more.

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss three problems that could slow Cameroon's progress towards emergence by 2035. (6 marks)
items.solution_markdown:
Award two marks for each problem that is explained, for example:
- Shortage of money: roads, dams and schools are costly, and funds may be limited, so projects are slow.
- Dependence on a few raw material exports: when world prices fall, earnings fall.
- Power cuts and poor roads: they raise costs and discourage investors.
- Corruption or insecurity: they reduce trust and investment.
- Unemployment among young people: it wastes talent and lowers demand.

**Three explained problems earn full marks; avoid taking political sides.**

items_markdown: Vision 2035 aims to make Cameroon an emerging country: less poverty, middle income, newly industrialised, and greater national unity and democracy.
The plan is carried out in stages through shorter strategies, with measures in industry, energy, minerals, transport, farming and training.
Energy efforts include hydroelectric dams and a gas power plant; mineral efforts include developing iron ore, bauxite and cobalt-nickel.
For each sector give an action and its result, and write as many points as the question asks.
Emergence is a target for 2035, not a finished fact.
